This limits downside squeeze risk but also means a sustained recovery needs spot demand, not just deleveraging.

mvrvSignal.cycleContext: In prior cycles, MVRV 1.3–1.6 during a mid-cycle correction has preceded strong recoveries when accompanied by accumulation signals. Currently, those accumulation signals (negative exchange netflow, ETF inflows) are ABSENT, so MVRV fair value is a floor indicator, not an immediate buy trigger. Watch for MVRV approaching 1.0–1.1 (near realized price ~$53,987) for high-conviction accumulation.

catalystWatch.event: 200d SMA Test ($73,190) — Phase A Re-entry Threshold
catalystWatch.note: Not a news event but the single most important technical catalyst this week. A daily close below $73,190 re-enters Phase A (ACCUMULATION) and triggers mandatory allocation rebalancing per firm mandate. A bounce and reclaim above $76,240 (7d VAL) would be the first signal of IMBALANCE_DOWN exhaustion. Market is at a decision point within 2–3 sessions.

brief.analystNote: BTC's -6.04% session on November 6 is a multi-factor stress event, not a single-catalyst flush: exchange inflows (+9,455 BTC, the largest normalized reading in today's data at 0.225% of liquid supply), ETF outflows at -$430M (-2.6x baseline), and LTH distribution at -8,438 BTC/day are firing simultaneously, while the auction market confirms IMBALANCE_DOWN with value migrating lower. The critical structural level is the 200d SMA at $73,190 — currently 3.1% below spot — which also marks the Phase A/B boundary; a confirmed daily close below this level would mandate a defensive posture reduction and suspension of new adds under the firm's phase protocol. Crucially, CME basis (+6.74% contango) and MVRV (1.398, fair value) are preventing this from being a sell-everything signal: institutional carry demand is intact and the market is not yet at the undervalued distress levels that historically define high-conviction macro entry points. The post-midterm regulatory overhang — Democrats shaping a market structure bill with expanded SEC oversight per [2026-11-04] Dcforecasts reporting — adds legislative uncertainty that institutional ETF allocators will price as a risk premium for at least 4–8 weeks. Market regime note: phase anchors are derived from 5-cycle history, below the statistical minimum for bear-realized (120) and bear-SMA (240) rules — treat current phase boundaries as heuristically reliable but not statistically robust, widening the confidence interval on Phase A/B transition levels by approximately ±$2,000.
brief.riskWarning: A daily close below $73,190 (200d SMA / Phase A floor) would invalidate the Phase B Breakout thesis, trigger the firm's allocation reduction protocol, and open a technical path toward the $65,000–$68,000 range where the next demand cluster is identifiable — this risk is 3.1% away and could materialize within 1–2 sessions given current exchange inflow and ETF outflow trajectory.
